home.headline: Rooted in Living Soil, Grown for Ecological Resilience.
home.subtitle: RootGuard is an open-source botanical journal and field companion for land stewards, farmers, and conservationists. We align resilient species selection with soil chemistry, track living specimens across parcels, and monitor longitudinal survival over quick planting counts.

ethos.quote: “A tree planted without regard to its companion microbiology and slope hydrology is an act of hope; a tree planted into living mycorrhizal mulch with contour swales is an act of engineering.”
ethos.text: Conventional reforestation initiatives report failure rates exceeding 70% within thirty months because success is measured by seedlings planted rather than mature canopy established. RootGuard introduces permanent geotagged check-ins and edaphic risk calculations to ensure accountability from initial root dip to decade-old crown.

speciesCare.sp001: Water regularly for first 6 months, drought-tolerant after. Requires full sun and deep well-draining soil pits.
speciesCare.sp002: Requires extensive root clearance. Water deeply during dry spells until aerial roots anchor into the topsoil.
speciesCare.sp003: Mulch root radius generously with dry leaves. Protect young grafts from direct hot winds in first two summers.
speciesCare.sp004: Thrives along stream banks and gully margins. Rapid rhizome development anchors steep, loose topsoil in 12 months.
speciesCare.sp005: Extremely sturdy pioneer tree; fissures in rocks provide root anchors. Minimal supplemental irrigation needed.
speciesCare.sp006: Produces vivid vermilion blooms. Plant in well-aerated soil; prune lower branches early for high canopy spread.
speciesCare.sp007: Forms a dense underground sponge network up to 3m deep within a year. Ideal for contour hedging and bund stabilization.
speciesCare.sp008: Requires well-drained fertile loam and moderate rainfall. Sheds foliage during dry season, reducing transpiration stress.
speciesCare.sp009: Tolerates waterlogging and riverbank silt. Deep taproot prevents high-velocity monsoon runoff scour.
speciesCare.sp010: Nitrogen-fixing legume adapted to saline and poor soils. Lateral roots form robust surface mats for slope retention.
speciesCare.sp011: Prodigious biomass generator. Highly resilient on alkaline road cuttings and dry barren embankments.
speciesCare.sp012: Porous riverbed alluvium preferred. Extensive root suckers help bind alluvial flood deposits.
speciesCare.sp013: Immense lifespan (>200 years) and deep wind-resistant taproot. Highly resistant to cyclonic gales.
speciesCare.sp014: Broad horizontal canopy with fragrant golden spherical flowers. Demands moist soil and full overhead sun.
speciesCare.sp015: Rapid growth; bears nutritious pods in first year. Prune top shoot at 1m to encourage branching.
speciesCare.sp016: High vitamin C fruit. Hardy against drought and moderate sodic soil salinity.
speciesCare.sp017: Signature riverbank guardian with buttressed trunk and pinkish-grey bark. Key for riparian buffer strips.
speciesCare.sp018: Popular agroforestry shade tree in hill plantations. Deep roots minimize competition with tea/coffee shrubs.
speciesCare.sp019: Thrives on dense black cotton clay and saline wastelands where most trees perish. Excellent firewood and soil binder.
speciesCare.sp020: Sacred tribal agroforestry anchor with rich succulent flowers. Vital component of dry deciduous forest restorations.
speciesCare.sp021: Endemic to dry hilly rocky terrains. Prefers well-drained red gravelly soils on gentle hill slopes.
speciesCare.sp022: Symbiotic actinomycetes fix atmospheric nitrogen in coastal sand dunes. Serves as front-line windbreak against sea storms.

soilTips.heading: Soil Health Tips
soilTips.subheading: Field-tested practices to rebuild topsoil humus, shield vulnerable ground horizons from thermal shock, and arrest monsoon runoff across watershed catchments.
soilTips.livingSoilDesc: One tablespoon of living soil contains more microorganisms than people on Earth. Preserve biological aggregation.

tip01.title: Composting Organic Biomass
tip01.paragraph: Healthy soil relies on an abundant community of mycorrhizal fungi, earthworms, and aerobic bacteria. Returning leaf litter, farm residues, and kitchen greens directly restores humus, unlocking locked trace minerals and improving crumb soil structure.
actions: Maintain a 30:1 carbon-to-nitrogen ratio using brown dry leaves and green clippings.
Aerate the pile bi-weekly to sustain aerobic fermentation and eliminate pathogens.
Incorporate 2–3 inches of mature dark compost into tree drip lines before monsoon planting.

tip02.title: Mulching Bare Soil
tip02.paragraph: Unshielded topsoil can exceed 48°C under direct sunlight, vaporizing subterranean moisture and sterilizing fragile soil biology. A generous organic mulch blanket stabilizes ground temperatures, suppresses weeds, and reduces irrigation demands by up to 60%.
actions: Apply a 3 to 4-inch layer of coarse woodchips, straw, or crushed sugarcane bagasse.
Keep mulch pulled back 3 inches from tree trunks to prevent fungal collar rot.
Replenish mulch carpets at the end of the monsoon to preserve residual profile moisture.

tip03.title: Slowing Runoff on Slopes
tip03.paragraph: High-velocity rainfall dislodges loose silt and carries nutrient-dense topsoil into drainage gullies. By sculpting contour swales, bunds, and vegetative check dams, water is slowed, spread, and encouraged to sink deep into groundwater aquifers.
actions: Survey precise contour lines with an A-frame before digging swales or planting ridges.
Plant vetiver grass or perennial shrubs along terrace edges to catch silt and bind soil.
Construct rock check dams in active hillside gullies to decelerate monsoon torrents.

tip04.title: Crop & Canopy Species Rotation
tip04.paragraph: Monocultures deplete specific root-zone nutrients and create localized disease reservoirs. Interplanting leguminous nitrogen fixers with deep-taprooted timber trees taps varied soil strata and naturally replenishes atmospheric nitrogen into the root zone.
actions: Pair heavy nitrogen consumers with leguminous nurse species such as Gliricidia or Subabul.
Alternate seasonal shallow-rooted cover crops with deep-rooting native perennials.
Avoid planting trees belonging to the same botanical family consecutively in the same pit.

tip05.title: Keeping Soil Permanently Covered
tip05.paragraph: Nature never leaves bare soil uncovered. Living roots pump liquid carbon exudates into the soil day and night, sustaining microbes and gluing silt particles into stable aggregates that resist wind deflation and torrential rain impact.
actions: Sow multi-species green manures (sunn hemp, cowpea, millet) during pre-monsoon showers.
Encourage low-growing native clover or creeping ground covers between tree sapling rows.
Never till or blade clear land prior to plantation; practice minimum soil disturbance.

tip06.title: Testing Soil Before Amending
tip06.paragraph: Blindly adding chemical fertilizers or lime can shift soil pH, lock up phosphorus, or induce salinity. Systematic soil testing identifies precise macronutrient deficiencies, cation exchange capacity, and organic carbon percentage before planting.
actions: Sample soil in a zigzag pattern across the parcel at both 0–15 cm and 15–30 cm depths.
Check pH levels: target 6.2–7.2 for general agroforestry; adjust acidic soils with dolomite.
Benchmark soil organic carbon (SOC); aim for >1.0% through perennial green biomass additions.

soilTips.footerManualText: Always correlate soil amendments with seasonal rainfall patterns. Incorporating raw green residues right before prolonged drought causes nitrogen immobilization; applying them 3 weeks prior to seasonal monsoons maximizes biological mineralization and sapling root vigor.

about.heading: Why Millions of Trees Are Planted, But Few Survive
about.subheading: Moving beyond token ceremonial planting days to genuine silvicultural survival and topsoil regeneration.
about.problemHeading: Most tree-planting initiatives fail because they celebrate seedlings put in the ground, not saplings that reach maturity.
about.problemP1: Around the globe, millions of saplings are planted each monsoon season in high-publicity drives. Yet global forestry research consistently shows that between 60% and 80% of unmonitored saplings perish within their first 18 months due to incorrect species placement, summer desiccation, livestock grazing, and soil erosion.
about.problemP2: RootGuard was engineered to transform planting from a fleeting public-relations event into a disciplined, data-verified discipline of stewardship.
about.toolsSubtitle: Every module in RootGuard tackles a specific breakdown point in conventional reforestation programs.

tenet1.title: Right Species, Right Soil
tenet1.desc: Botanical compatibility prevents planting water-demanding or fragile trees into alkaline or thin rocky slopes.

tenet2.desc: Check-in logs track height growth, crown spread, and weed competition across month 1, 6, 12, and 24.

tenet3.title: Soil Conservation as Priority
tenet3.desc: Saplings act as anchor pins; without contour swales and living organic mulches, seedlings wash away in monsoon deluges.

tenet4.desc: Publicly verifiable QR codes and coordinate ledgers allow any field auditor to verify tree vitality on the ground.
